authority: Record Clearing Implementation Authority Reconciled (2026-08-24), Completed Decision Matrix — P0 decisions and effective-date-gated routes

routes.mechanism: Record restriction for qualifying nonconvictions from arrests on or after July 1, 2013

timing.anchorText: handled through the prosecutor and GCIC process without a participant waiting period

exclusions: Separate post-July 1, 2013 nonconviction, pardoned-felony, and first-offender mechanisms
Apply July 1, 2026 first-offender law prospectively as written
routes.notes: Status, correction and prosecutor-contact guidance. Do not sell a court packet unless a statutory judicial-review path is actually triggered.

routes.mechanism: Restriction and sealing of a pardoned felony

timing.anchorText: available after the pardon issues; there is no separate post-pardon elapsed wait

exclusions: Separate post-July 1, 2013 nonconviction, pardoned-felony, and first-offender mechanisms
Apply July 1, 2026 first-offender law prospectively as written
routes.packetFamily: Georgia Restriction and Sealing Petition for a Pardoned Felony under § 35-3-37
routes.notes: Statutory exclusions, the no-disqualifying-later-conviction rule, the no-pending-charge rule, and the balancing requirement must all be met.

routes.mechanism: First-offender restriction and sealing under the July 1, 2026 amendments

timing.anchorText: restriction and sealing are addressed at sentencing or disposition under the amended process; older first-offender records use the applicable retroactive petition or correction mechanism

exclusions: Separate post-July 1, 2013 nonconviction, pardoned-felony, and first-offender mechanisms
Apply July 1, 2026 first-offender law prospectively as written
routes.packetFamily: Georgia First-Offender Restriction and Sealing Petition under § 42-8-62.1
routes.notes: The intake must branch explicitly on the July 1, 2026 statutory change; apply the new law prospectively as written.

routes.mechanism: First-time drug offender expungement after treatment and dismissal

timing.anchorText: event-triggered on successful treatment or probation completion, discharge, and dismissal; no additional ordinary waiting period applies

routes.packetFamily: Hawaii First-Time Drug Offender Expungement Order Request under § 706-622.5
packetComponents: Request for the statutory expungement order
routes.notes: No ordinary waiting period is added after successful discharge and dismissal.

routes.mechanism: Nonconviction arrest expungement through the Attorney General

timing.anchorText: generally available on a qualifying nonconviction disposition, with two coded statutory exceptions: one year after discharge or dismissal in the specified deferred-acceptance branch, and five years in the specified petty-misdemeanor or violation bail-forfeiture branch

processingDeadlines.label: Attorney General processing period
processingDeadlines.note: agency processing after the application, not a filing wait

routes.packetFamily: Hawaii Attorney General Expungement Application under § 831-3.2
packetComponents: Written application to the Attorney General
routes.notes: Since July 1, 2025 the Attorney General process also addresses related court-record removal under the one-step procedure. The one-year deferred-acceptance and five-year bail-forfeiture exceptions must be coded separately and never applied to the general branch.

timing.anchorText: not less than one year after the person's twenty-first birthday

exclusions: Route-specific completion, clean-record, excluded-offense, and frequency conditions
routes.notes: The age-21 clock is its own rule object and must never share a rule with the § 610.140 completion clock. Subject to the first-offense, later-alcohol-record, commercial-driver and other statutory conditions.

routes.mechanism: General expungement of an arrest, charge, plea, trial, or conviction

timing.anchorText: one year for a misdemeanor, municipal offense or infraction and three years for a felony, measured from completion of the disposition or sentence and satisfaction of the statute; the arrest-only or no-charge branch uses the separate eighteen-month statutory anchor

exclusions: Route-specific completion, clean-record, excluded-offense, and frequency conditions
routes.notes: One year, three years and eighteen months are three separate branches keyed to offense level and the arrest-only condition; the stored value is the misdemeanor branch and the exact branch is a mandatory intake fact.

routes.mechanism: Marijuana expungement — automatic constitutional processing for completed and nonincarcerated cases

timing.anchorText: the constitutional processing mandate applies; no ordinary elapsed waiting period is used

exclusions: Qualifying marijuana conduct within Article XIV quantity/offense limits and not within constitutional exclusions
routes.notes: Do not sell a routine § 610.140 packet for a constitutionally automatic marijuana record. Where the record remains, give status and correction or escalation guidance. A person currently incarcerated for conduct made lawful uses the Article XIV petition for vacatur, release and expungement; no general one- or three-year § 610.140 period applies to that branch either.
